name: Shackleton Crater Rim
description: High ridge along the rim of Shackleton Crater. Features extended periods of solar illumination (~86% annually) and immediate access to ultra-cold permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) inside the crater floor.
scientific_interest: Volatiles prospecting, cryogenic ice preservation, continuous solar power generation.
primary_advantages: High solar illumination
Near-permanent radio line of sight to Earth during favorable libration
Proximal PSR volatile access
primary_challenges: Extreme thermal gradients between sunlit rim and shadow

name: Connecting Ridge
description: Topographic elevated ridge bridging Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. One of the prime landing zones identified by NASA Artemis planners due to benign slopes and extended illumination windows.
scientific_interest: Geomorphology of highland impact structures, continuous solar-powered operations, mobility corridor.
primary_advantages: Gentle terrain suitable for precision landers
High cumulative sunlight (~82%)
Traversable corridor for uncrewed rovers
primary_challenges: Periodic solar occultations by de Gerlache massif
Earth visibility fluctuations during lunar libration

name: Malapert Mountain (Massif)
description: Towering 5-kilometer high topographic massif named after Charles Malapert. Because of its sheer altitude and position, it enjoys near-continuous direct line-of-sight to Earth, making it the premier telecommunication and relay base.
scientific_interest: Lunar communications relay site, astronomical observatories, deep-crustal lunar sample return.
primary_advantages: Near-uninterrupted line-of-sight to Earth (DTE)
Excellent long-distance visibility for radio telemetry
Elevated solar horizon above local terrain
primary_challenges: High local topography requires specialized descent trajectory
Distance from polar water-ice traps is greater than ultra-polar sites

name: de Gerlache Rim 1
description: Broad elevated plateau on the southern rim of de Gerlache crater. Exhibits smooth landing terrain with minimal hazardous boulder concentrations identified in LROC Narrow Angle Camera imagery.
scientific_interest: Pre-Nectarian impact geology, low-risk autonomous landing demonstration, subsurface drill targets.
primary_advantages: Low average slope (<6°)
Stable thermal environment on plateau
Good Earth communication window during southern libration
primary_challenges: Shadow periods up to 55 consecutive hours during lunar winter
Requires robust battery storage or mini-RTG power backup

name: Haworth Crater Rim
description: Sunlit ridge overlooking Haworth Crater, one of the coldest known regions in the Solar System according to NASA Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment measurements (<40 Kelvin in deep shadow).
scientific_interest: Thermal extreme measurements, hydrogen neutron spectroscopy anomalies, cold-trapped volatiles.
primary_advantages: Proximity to ultra-cold deep PSRs with confirmed neutron absorption signatures
High science value for resource prospecting
primary_challenges: Complex horizon profile with multiple ridge obstructions
Steep crater descent slopes (>20°) requiring tethered rovers

name: Nobile Rim (VIPER Landing Site)
description: Selected landing site for NASA VIPER (Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover). Features rolling hills, accessible micro-cold traps, and validated safe landing corridors mapped at sub-meter resolution.
scientific_interest: Direct measurement of subsurface volatiles, water ice ground-truth validation for orbital neutron detectors.
primary_advantages: Extensively characterized landing corridors
Very low slope gradient (~4.8°)
Moderate shadow durations matching rover battery capacity
primary_challenges: Periodic solar shadow requires opportunistic traverses
Communication outages when terrain dips below Earth line of sight

name: Amundsen Crater Rim
description: Large impact basin rim with ancient uplifted anorthositic materials. Offers large open landing spots with clear line of sight and moderate surface roughness.
scientific_interest: Early lunar crust composition, impact melt dating, transitions between polar and equatorial regolith.
primary_advantages: Large unobstructed landing ellipses (>1 km radius)
Good visibility to Earth communication network
Stable regolith geotechnical properties
primary_challenges: Longer winter shadow intervals due to lower latitude compared to Shackleton
Higher thermal variation during diurnal cycle

name: Leibnitz Plateau
description: High-altitude plateau on the outer rings of the immense South Pole-Aitken (SPA) basin. Pristine mantle and deep crust materials exposed by ancient mega-impact.
scientific_interest: Sampling the deepest excavated lunar materials to unlock the early history of the Solar System.
primary_advantages: Vast flat highland topography
Direct line-of-sight to Earth for majority of the month
High elevation above local obstruction planes
primary_challenges: Higher radiation exposure due to highland summit exposure
Lower concentration of surface volatile traps
